meta.title: Post-war regime transitions, partitions and state dissolution, 1944–1999
meta.scope: Research staging for Eastern Europe, dissolution of the USSR and Yugoslavia, Czechoslovakia, Korea, Vietnam and the ROC relocation/PRC foundation. Dates are legal/proclamation milestones unless otherwise noted; not every transition implies instant full territorial control or completed democratization.
meta.schemaNote: Uses CG-41 event fields and adds optional culturalAssignments for dominant titular culture map-splitting hints. Entity IDs not in historical_data/political_entities/registry.json are proposed research IDs. regionIds are suggestions only where explicitly supplied; empty arrays mean no safe crosswalk was established.
meta.dateConvention: ISO-8601 Gregorian. For processes, note declaration date separately from legal effectiveness. Military demarcation lines are not permanent borders.

qualityLegend.verified: Primary law, official archive or UN legal document directly confirms the date or legal act.
qualityLegend.supported: Official institutional chronology or credible historical synthesis supports the event; details may need primary legal verification.
qualityLegend.unverified: Not used as a positive event assertion; gaps are stated explicitly.

meta.entityIdWarning: Most post-1945 states (POL-PRL, HUN-PEOPLE, CZE, ROM, BUL, YUG-FPR, YUG-SFR, ALB, USSR, LTU, GEO, EST, LVA, UKR, BLR, MDA, AZE, UZB, KGZ, ARM, TJK, TKM, KAZ, RUS-FED, CIS, MKD, BIH, YUG-FRY, SVK, ROK, PRK, DRV, SVN, RVN, PRG, VNM-SRV, ROC, PRC) require checking/mapping against the current entity registry before integration.
meta.mapSplitWarning: The 1836 map contains coarse regions. Korea's KOR_HAM and Vietnam's VNM_HUE straddle the 38th/17th parallel respectively; the data marks approximate splits and must not be applied as exact ownership patches without subdividing those regions.
meta.culturalAssignmentWarning: Dominant culture is a map allocation key, not a claim of ethnic homogeneity. Preserve minority cultures, mixed regions, and historic diasporas; do not overwrite every province with the titular group.

entityAfter.name_vi: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa và giới tuyến quân sự tạm thời

causes: Geneva Conference agreements ended the First Indochina War
Temporary military demarcation near the 17th parallel pending nationwide elections
events.note: The 17th-parallel line was explicitly provisional and not a political or territorial boundary. Region mapping is approximate: VNM_HUE straddles the line and must be split; do not use this as a permanent border event.

entityBefore.name_vi: Quốc gia Việt Nam

causes: Bảo Đại removed following referendum and Ngô Đình Diệm consolidated power
Republic proclaimed 26 October 1955

power.note: Republican form did not imply competitive liberal democracy; the Diệm presidency concentrated executive authority.

events.note: Separate the State of Vietnam (1949–1955) from the Republic of Vietnam (1955–1975); both used Saigon as capital.

entityBefore.name_vi: Việt Nam Cộng hòa

entityAfter.name_en: Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam
entityAfter.name_vi: Chính phủ Cách mạng lâm thời Cộng hòa miền Nam Việt Nam

causes: Fall of Saigon and surrender of the Republic of Vietnam government
Provisional Revolutionary Government assumed authority in the South pending reunification

territorialChanges.note: Do not mark formal state reunification on this date.

events.note: 30 April 1975 marks the collapse of the RVN government and transfer of control; legal reunification occurred later.

entityBefore.name_vi: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Xã hội chủ nghĩa Việt Nam

causes: First session of the unified National Assembly
National Assembly resolution adopted 2 July 1976

territorialChanges.note: The 17th-parallel military line ceased to divide the state; retain separate region identities and cultural minorities.

events.note: The National Assembly resolution explicitly names the unified state Socialist Republic of Vietnam and Hanoi as capital; the official archive identifies the original National Assembly file.

entityBefore.name_en: Republic of China government on the mainland
entityBefore.name_vi: Chính phủ Trung Hoa Dân Quốc trên đại lục

entityAfter.name_en: Republic of China government relocated to Taiwan
entityAfter.name_vi: Chính phủ Trung Hoa Dân Quốc chuyển sang Đài Loan

causes: Communist victory on the mainland and establishment of the PRC on 1 October 1949
ROC Executive Yuan moved its effective seat to Taipei on 9 December 1949
events.note: The ROC did not become a new state in 1949; its government relocated to Taiwan. Taipei was the effective seat of government, while ROC constitutional claims to China continued. Do not treat this as a universally settled sovereignty transfer over Taiwan.

entityBefore.name_en: Republic of China on mainland China
entityBefore.name_vi: Trung Hoa Dân Quốc trên đại lục

entityAfter.name_vi: Cộng hòa Nhân dân Trung Hoa

causes: Chinese Communist Party victory in the Chinese Civil War on the mainland
Proclamation of the PRC on 1 October 1949
events.note: The PRC was established on the mainland while the ROC government continued in Taiwan; this is a competing-government and territorial-control transition, not an uncontested single-state rename.
